label: New Jazz (Prestige)
rationale: Dolphy's second leader date and the first full statement of his mature, chord-less concept: cello-and-bass front line (Ron Carter in one of his first recorded appearances, George Duvivier), no piano, Roy Haynes driving. Five-star AllMusic review ('a depth and purpose that were unprecedented and remain singularly unique'), five-star Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide, 3.5-star Penguin Guide. Lineage signal: the explicit bridge from Chico Hamilton's cello ensembles through Dolphy's Mingus years toward Out to Lunch! (already in the canon); James Newton cites this record's flute work as formative. Wikipedia tags it avant-garde/third stream/post-bop — proposed as post-bop leaning scope_call for John to weigh how far toward the free-jazz boundary this sits. scope_check.boundary_note: Year is safely inside 1940–1979; the live boundary is the avant-garde / post-bop edge — Wikipedia tags the album avant-garde and third stream, and the rubric's borderline modal/avant rule (Out to Lunch!, The Shape of Jazz to Come) applies directly here.

ballot.case_for: This is the first full statement of Dolphy's mature chordless concept — cello-and-bass front line, no piano — recorded four years before Out to Lunch! (already in the canon) and functioning as the explicit lineage bridge from Chico Hamilton's cello ensembles through Dolphy's Mingus years (James Newton cites its flute work as formative). Consensus is strong across independent reference works: 5 stars from AllMusic ('a depth and purpose that were unprecedented and remain singularly unique') and 5 stars from the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide, with 3.5 from the Penguin Guide. Session gravity is exceptional: one of Ron Carter's first recorded appearances, George Duvivier, Roy Haynes, Rudy Van Gelder at the board. And it passes the discovery test vividly — the timbral identity of cello as highest voice with no chordal instrument remains singular in the entire catalog.
ballot.case_against: The album's angular, harmonically ungrounded language leans well past the canon's hard-bop/modal center of gravity, and John's standing free-jazz taste note ('studying it rather than dismissing it') means this chordless chamber-avant texture will test what actually resonates with him. The consensus, while real, is not overwhelming: the rigorous Penguin Guide stops at 3.5 stars, and no Penguin Core Collection, NPR, or DownBeat canon-list citation is in evidence — the case rests on star ratings and a Wikipedia synthesis, with a recorded metadata conflict on the release date. Finally, with Out to Lunch! already carrying Dolphy's definitive avant-garde statement in the canon, this record can be read as the developmental step toward it rather than a load-bearing pillar in its own right.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes John rule on the avant-garde boundary: both references independently tier this scope_call at strong priority — a singular, lineage-bridging Dolphy record whose chordless abstraction only he can weigh against his free-jazz calibration.
